notes: Stock rows are additive lots: aggregate 'Quantity pieces' by material code and warehouse to produce one inventory entry per warehouse; do not sum BKK and CNX together.
Material code values are zero-padded identifiers (for example 000001) even though the profiler types the column as integer; they should be preserved as strings.
The Price sheet explicitly carries THB for all rows, so the currency is source-supported rather than inferred.
Join Stock and Price to the Material master on Material code; the Material and Price sheets each contain 12 unique material codes, while Stock contains 12 codes across 2 warehouses.

tables.reason: One row per material code (12 distinct codes across 12 rows), each with a unique product description; this is the product master list.

columns.name: Material code
columns.reason: Unique material identifier with one value per product and zero-padded display values such as 000001; must be preserved as text.

columns.name: Description
columns.reason: Unique descriptive product name per material code, such as 'Coffee variant 01' or 'Soap variant 11'.

tables.reason: 24 stock rows covering 12 material codes in two warehouses (BKK and CNX); rows are additive stock lots keyed by material code plus warehouse.

columns.name: Material code
columns.reason: Foreign key to the Material master; each code appears twice because stock is split across the two warehouses.

columns.name: Warehouse
columns.reason: Two warehouse identifiers, BKK and CNX, each repeated for all 12 materials; this is the inventory entry identity.

columns.name: Quantity pieces
columns.reason: Stock quantity in individual pieces per material and warehouse lot; values must be summed within each warehouse, never across warehouses.

tables.reason: One selling price and one currency per unique material code across 12 rows; this is the price list.

columns.name: Material code
columns.reason: Unique material identifier linking each price row to the product master.

columns.name: Selling price
columns.reason: Positive selling price values from 113 to 256, one per material; target requires requested selling price rather than cost.

columns.name: Currency
columns.reason: Single explicit source currency value THB for every price row; no currency inference needed.

changes_from_draft: Root record switched to the Material master sheet (source 'products') so the master product population and Description drive /sku and /product_name; the Price sheet is now a 1:1 left join (source 'prices').
Added /product_name from Material 'Description' — the field was missing in the draft.
Fixed collection item pointers to the catalogue paths /inventory/*/warehouse_code and /inventory/*/qty (bare /warehouse_code and /qty were rejected).

Built the /inventory collection from the Stock sheet with link on Material code and aggregate group_by /warehouse_code, sum /qty — lots are summed within each warehouse and BKK/CNX are never added together.
/sku now preserves the zero-padded 6-digit code (strip leading zeros then re-pad via regex) instead of normalize_whitespace, which risked losing leading zeros.
Join and collection key matching normalised with trim + strip_leading_zeros so '000001' and '1' link correctly.

Dropped the restrictive file name_patterns ((?i)^balances, (?i)^selling_prices) and bind sources by sheet name so the Material/Stock/Price sheets resolve regardless of which uploaded workbook carries them.
Currency mapping simplified to upper/trim plus a small keep-unmapped value map; all 12 rows already state THB explicitly.
Removed the draft's open questions about SKU identity and a missing quantity column — the Material master identity and the 'Quantity pieces' column are established by the sheets.

agent_log.basis: complete execution, populated source-backed fields and unique identities
retired: No SKU-like header found in root table; using 'Material code' as identity — confirm
Inventory table 'Stock' has no recognisable quantity column
